key_insight: ADACT jointly optimizes workload throttling and cooling using a physics-based thermal PDE to balance temperature risk, cooling energy, and processor throughput.
engineering_relevance: The approach offers predictive thermal management for power-dense AI and HPC processors by coordinating software workloads with hardware cooling.
method: Model chip temperature with a 2D reaction–diffusion PDE, localized power sources, and variable cooling.
Discretize with second-order Crank–Nicolson time stepping and a five-point finite-difference Laplacian.
Use backward adjoint gradients and L-BFGS to optimize workload and cooling controls.
evidence_signal: Manufactured-solution tests verify second-order state and adjoint convergence, Taylor tests validate gradients, and numerical experiments report thermal-threshold compliance while maintaining throughput.
watch_item: The abstract reports numerical validation, not deployment on physical processors; real-world performance depends on thermal-model calibration and control-loop cost.
paper_title: ADACT: PDE-Constrained Thermal Hardware/Software Co-Design Adjoint-Driven Optimal Control via Finite Difference Discretization
